chapters_cited.topics: Examination of ground by tactile feel, sound, color, smell, taste, slope (Plava), and compaction (Garta-pūraṇa). Method of digging a 1-cubit pit and refilling with soil; testing water absorption overnight.
chapters_cited.sanskrit_reference: arocanīyā bhūmir varṇair gandhai rasaiḥ padaiḥ | parīkṣya kuryāt sarveṣāṃ vāstūnāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ viduḥ ||

chapters_cited.topics: Ritual ploughing (Karṣaṇa) with white bulls, offering of oblations (Bali), soil levelling, extraction of subterranean debris (Śalya-śodhana: bones, charcoal, roots).

Mathematical determination of True East-West (Prācī) and North-South (Udīcī) using shadow-circle intersections (Chāyā-bhramaṇa) of a 12-angula or 24-angula gnomon. Distinction between cardinal plots (Sama-dig) and tilted/diagonal plots (Vidiśa).

Slope categorization: Supraśastā (declining East or North) vs Apasavyā and Adhama. 16 Canonical plot shapes: Caturasra (Square), Āyatasra (Rectangle), Gomukha (Cow-face), Śārdūlamukha (Lion-face), Trikoṇa (Triangle), Vṛtta (Circle), Hastipṛṣṭha (Elephant-back), Kūrmapṛṣṭha (Tortoise-back), Daityapṛṣṭha (Demon-back).
chapters_cited.sanskrit_reference: prāg-udaṅ-nimnā supraśastā savya-nimnā ca śasyate | viparītā tu na śastā sarva-sampatti-nāśinī ||

chapters_cited.topics: Method of establishing the cardinal axes using gnomonic shadows, corrections for solar declination (Kṣiti-valaya), and ensuring plot orthogonality.

Classification of soil characteristics for social groups (Varnas/Guṇas); Garta-pūraṇa compaction test; Jala-parīkṣā; Plot slopes (Indra-vīthi, Yama-vīthi, Varuṇa-vīthi, Soma-vīthi); Street thrusts (Vīthi-śūla) and surrounding road networks.
chapters_cited.sanskrit_reference: śveta-raktā-pīta-kṛṣṇā brāhmaṇāder hitā mahī | madhura-kaṣāyāmlā-katu-rasā kramāc ca smṛtā || gartaṃ pūrayet tadvad dravyādhikya-samam hīnam |

chapters_cited.topics: Four classical topographic profiles: Gajapṛṣṭha (Elephant back - high in SW/S/W, low in NE/N/E, yields maximum longevity and wealth), Kūrmapṛṣṭha (Tortoise back - elevated center, gentle perimeter slope, grants stability and spiritual peace), Daityapṛṣṭha (Demon back - high in NE, low in SW, leads to ruin and lineage extinction), Nāgapṛṣṭha (Serpent back - undulating, high E-W, low N-S, causes constant wandering and demise).
Street layouts, avoidance of Marma-vedha, road frontal hierarchy, and environmental wind channelization.

chapters_cited.topics: Scholarly comparative synthesis of Aparājitapṛcchā, Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra, and Mayamata; geotechnical load-bearing interpretations of classical soil compaction tests; cosmological and solar rationale behind North-East decline.

inputs.name: Plot Geometry / Shape
inputs.description: Geometric morphology of the boundary perimeter as surveyed on site.

inputs.name: Length to Width Ratio (Proportion)
inputs.description: Proportion of plot length to width (Length / Width). Ideal is 1:1 (Square) or 1:1.25 to 1:1.5 (Auspicious Rectangle). Ratios beyond 1:2.0 represent Dirgha-shala / excessive elongation.

inputs.name: Natural Slope / Terrain Gradient
inputs.description: Dominant natural downward slope of the terrain surface.

inputs.name: Broad Geological Contour (Bhūmi-Pṛṣṭha)
inputs.description: Macro-topography of the terrain according to classical taxonomy: Gajapṛṣṭha (high in S/W/SW, low in N/E/NE), Kūrmapṛṣṭha (high center, low periphery), Daityapṛṣṭha (high in N/E/NE, low in S/W/SW), Nāgapṛṣṭha (undulating E-W ridges).

inputs.name: Soil Color (Excavated Strata)
inputs.description: Color of virgin subsoil at 1 cubit depth. Classically associated with Guṇa and suitability.

inputs.name: Soil Odor / Smell
inputs.description: Olfactory test of moist virgin soil. Foul odors indicate decomposing organic matter, shallow water table, or toxic chemical strata.

inputs.name: Compaction Pit Test (Garta-Pūraṇa)
inputs.description: A 1-cubit (approx. 18-24 inches) cubic pit is dug and the excavated soil is poured back without manual tamping. Surplus earth indicates dense preconsolidated soil (high bearing capacity); sunken deficit indicates loose, porous, collapsable soil.

inputs.name: Water Percolation & Retention Test (Jala-Parīkṣā)
inputs.description: The excavated pit is filled with water at sunset and inspected at dawn. Substantial retained water demonstrates cohesive impermeable strata; bone-dry cracked ground indicates excessive void ratio, fissures, or subterranean cavities.

inputs.name: Primary Road Facing / Frontage
inputs.description: Direction from which primary access road fronts the property.

inputs.name: Street Focus / T-Junction Thrust (Vīthi-Śūla)
inputs.description: Presence and orientation of an oncoming road terminating directly perpendicular to the plot boundary.

inputs.name: Deviation Angle from Geographic North (Śaṅku Dig-Nirṇaya)
inputs.description: Angular tilt of the plot's primary axis relative to true magnetic/geographic North. Plots with 0-5° are Cardinal (Sama-dig); >15° are Vidiśa (Diagonal).

inputs.name: Corner Extensions & Cuts (Koṇa-Vṛddhi / Kartana)
inputs.description: Structural deviation from 90° orthogonality at the plot corners.

formula_logic.mathematical_formula: CPVSI = Clamp[0, 100, (w_shape * S_shape + w_slope * S_slope + w_soil * S_soil + w_orient * S_orient + w_road * S_road) * Product(M_penalties)]

scoring_scale.0_39: Varjita (Prohibited / Defective / Unfit for residence without complete re-structuring)

rules_matrix.element_mahabhuta: Prithvi & Akasha (Equilibrium of all five Mahābhūtas)
rules_matrix.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 12; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 14; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 85
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: caturaśrā sarveṣāṃ vāstūnāṃ śubhadā sadā | sarva-kāma-phalā nṝṇāṃ dhana-dhānya-vivardhinī ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: A square plot has four equal sides and four 90° right angles. It establishes complete energetic symmetry and balance of the cardinal poles, granting holistic health, mental clarity, and enduring wealth.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Perfect geometric symmetry eliminates torsional moments during seismic events, ensures equal daylight distribution, and optimizes structural load paths.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: None required. Consecrate the central Brahmasthāna as an open-to-sky courtyard or lightweight zone.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 13; Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 22; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 16
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: āyatā śubhadā nityaṃ catur-varga-phala-pradā | dīrghatve dvy-ardha-mātraṃ tu śastam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: An oblong rectangular plot with length-to-width ratio between 1:1.25 and 1:1.50, aligned North-South or East-West, is highly auspicious, bestowing success in worldly affairs and long life.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Optimal aspect ratio facilitates natural cross-ventilation, clear spatial zoning between public and private domains, and efficient plumbing distribution.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Ensure the ratio does not exceed 1:2. If ratio is greater than 2:1, divide the plot physically or energetically using compound walls or hedging.

rules_matrix.direction_zone: Front facing East or North; Broad in Rear (West/South)
rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 34; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 24
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: gomukhaṃ tu sadā śastaṃ gṛheṣu dhanavardhanam | paścādvistīrṇamagre tu saṅkṣiptaṃ gomukhaṃ smṛtam ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Narrow in the front (road side) and broad in the back. When the narrow front faces East or North and the broad back rests in South or West, it forms the sacred Gomukhi configuration, accumulating and preserving family wealth and harmony.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Funnel geometry acts as an acoustic and aerodynamic buffer against front street dust and noise while maximizing quiet, private open space in the rear.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: If the front faces South or West, it reverses the polarity; correct by planting dense bamboo/ficus hedges in the front and keeping the rear open.

rules_matrix.direction_zone: Front facing North/East; Narrow in Rear
rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 35; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 16
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: vyāghra-vaktre tu vāṇijyaṃ rāja-saṃsevane hitam | vāsārthaṃ naiva kartavyaṃ putradāra-vināśanam ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Broad at the front and narrow at the rear. Auspicious for commercial ventures, corporate headquarters, public retail, or administrative buildings, but prohibited for domestic residences as it disperses domestic tranquility.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Wide street frontage provides excellent visual exposure, branding frontage, and ingress capacity for commercial foot traffic, but compromises residential privacy.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: For residential use on a Shermukhi plot, construct a straight boundary wall to partition off the irregular triangular side wedges, rendering the habitable plot a true rectangle.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 87; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 28; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 17
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: trikoṇe vahnibhītiḥ syād rāja-daṇḍas tathaiva ca | kulanāśo bhavet tatra na kuryāt tatra mandiram ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Triangular plots generate aggressive angular convergence (Agni-koṇa dynamics), predisposing occupants to constant litigation, fire accidents, internal bickering, and royal/governmental penalties.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Acute corner angles (<60°) produce severe internal stress concentrations, dead unusable corners with stagnant air, and complicated structural roof framing.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Erect internal perimeter walls or heavy evergreen hedges to carve out an internal square or rectangle, relegating the triangular acute corners to external landscaped gardens with a dedicated Agni yantra.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 30; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 18; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 14
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: vṛttā tu yā mahī loke sā śastā suraveśmani | narāṇāṃ na hitā sā hi dāridrya-maraṇāvahā ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Circular plots lack stabilizing cardinal corners. Classical treatises permit circular plots solely for circular temples, Buddhist stupas, civic amphitheaters, or ascetic hermitages; residential use causes poverty and lack of foundation.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Curvilinear boundaries make standard orthogonal construction uneconomical and generate unstable acoustic reflections focusing sound towards the center.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Square off the living compound inside the circle by creating four corner landscape gardens.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 32; Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 38
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: viṣama-bāhuṣu nityaṃ śatrubhītiḥ prajāyate | dravyasaṅkṣayaḥ kalahaḥ syād vāstudoṣeṇa sarvadā ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Plots with unequal non-parallel sides and asymmetric corner angles cause chaotic energy distribution, leading to perpetual enemy fear, unexpected financial drain, and discord among partners.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Irregular boundaries generate asymmetric seismic torsional shears and complicate structural alignment.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Survey the plot, establish an orthogonal rectangle inside, and surrender the residual irregular margins to outer compound greenery or parking.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 20; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 26
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: śakaṭākṛti-yā bhūmiḥ sā sarvārtha-vināśinī | nṛṇāṃ dāridryadā nityaṃ pravāsa-maraṇa-pradā ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Shaped like a bullock cart (narrow in middle, wide at front and back), it forces continuous wandering, severe financial penury, and premature loss of family heads.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Constricted central waist restricts airflow, utilities, and emergency egress routes between front and back zones.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Straighten the waist with compound boundary adjustments or partition into two separate self-contained rectangular units.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 30; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 5; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 88
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: īśāna-plavanā bhūmiḥ sarvasiddhividhāyinī | āyur-ārogya-sampattir vijayo vṛddhir uttamā ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: A plot sloping down towards the North-East (Īśāna-plava) is the supreme topographical contour. It allows uninterrupted absorption of early morning ultraviolet-enriched solar radiation and magnetic flux, bestowing health, intellect, and spiritual and material abundance.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Natural surface runoff discharges towards the NE corner, allowing clean stormwater gravity disposal without contaminating southern living zones.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: None needed. Keep this lowest quadrant clean, open, and free of massive masonry loads.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 30; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 45
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: pūrva-plavā vṛddhikarī sarva-sampat-pradāyinī | sūrya-tejo-samāyuktā kuloddhāra-karī sadā ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: An Eastward slope (Pūrva-plava / Indra-vīthi) welcomes the rising sun across the site, promoting physical vitality, professional status, enlightenment, and harmonious governance.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Maximizes passive solar heat gain in winter mornings while enabling rapid drying of nocturnal dampness.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Maintain low boundary wall on East and higher boundary wall on West.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 30; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 6
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: dhanadā cottarā plavā vidyā-dhana-samṛddhidā | kauberasya prasādena kīrti-sampad-vivardhinī ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: A Northward slope (Uttara-plava / Soma-vīthi) draws the Earth's geomagnetic lines of force freely across the plot, conferring wealth, career advancements, intellectual sharpness, and commercial success.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Shielded from harsh southern glare while receiving continuous diffused ambient northern light (ideal for studies and studios).
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Keep Northern perimeter open with light permeable railings.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 49; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 8
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: nairṛtyāṃ ca duryogaḥ kulanāśaḥ prajāyate | dāridryaṃ vyādhi-saṃpāto mṛtyur vā maraṇāntikam ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: A downward slope towards the South-West (Nairṛtya-plava / Daityapṛṣṭha) is a catastrophic defect. It exposes the vulnerable southwest to drainage erosion while depressing the earth element, resulting in chronic health crises, bankruptcy, addiction, and premature demise of the head of the house.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Causes heavy stormwater to pool in the SW, weakening foundation soils under maximum afternoon thermal expansion and leading to differential settlement.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Extensive civil engineering earthwork: fill the SW quadrant with compacted gravel/earth to make it the highest elevation; construct heavy retaining walls and terrace slopes toward the North-East.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 89
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: dakṣiṇa-plavā mṛtyukārī vartanāśī vināśinī | vyādhi-śokākulā nityaṃ nārīṇāṃ ca vināśanī ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Sloping down to the South drains vital life force into the realm of Yama, causing chronic illnesses, blood disorders, legal persecution, and premature decline of female family members.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Southern drainage often leads to thermal overheating and excessive desiccation of exposed soil slopes during summer months.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Build a high, massive southern compound wall; install heavy landscaping boulders in the South to artificially elevate and anchor the terrain.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 7
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: vartanāśī ca paścimā putrahāni-karī smṛtā | dravyasaṅkṣaya-kāriṇī pravāsa-jananī sadā ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: A Westward slope causes ongoing financial drain, delayed achievements, and children abandoning home.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Direct exposure of downward slopes to blazing western afternoon infrared radiation creates severe microclimate heat buildup.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Elevate western plinth with retaining walls and plant tall shade trees (e.g. Ashoka, Neem) along the western boundary.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 90
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: āgneyyāṃ dāha-santāpo rājadveṣas tathaiva ca | putra-mitra-kalatraiś ca virodho jāyate mahān ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Sloping down to the South-East fuels unrestrained fire energy, leading to accidental fires, electrical breakdowns, anger issues, and high medical expenses.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Creates an undesirable drainage runoff trap adjacent to kitchen/utility zones.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Backfill SE to make it higher than the NE/North; install a copper swastika or copper rod grid in the SE corner.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 51
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: vāyavyāṃ roga-uccāṭam aśāntir dhana-saṅkṣayaḥ | cañcalā sampado nityaṃ bāndhava-dveṣa eva ca ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Sloping down to the North-West causes wind-element instability, mental restlessness, insomnia, strained neighborly ties, and chronic respiratory or nervous conditions.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Funneling of chilly prevailing northwest winter winds into a depression causes dampness and energy loss.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Level the NW; plant wind-breaking trees and install brass/silver energy harmonizers.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 40; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 10
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: kūrmapṛṣṭhā samākhyātā madhye tūnnatasaṃsthitā | sarva-sampat-karī nṝṇāṃ sthirāyur-dhana-vardhinī ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Center elevated with gentle slopes outward like a tortoise shell (Kūrmapṛṣṭha). Promotes longevity, emotional stability, and robust financial accumulation.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Prevents stormwater from ponding near the building foundation, draining natural runoff outward to municipal perimeters.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Channel the perimeter drainage so that it collects and exits predominantly through the North-East.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 42; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 92
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: madhye nimnā mahī yā syād gartā sarvavināśinī | tasyāṃ vāso na kartavyo dāridrya-kalanāvahaḥ ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Center sunken with perimeter elevated creates a basin or crater (Raurava / Garta). It collapses the Brahmasthāna, inflicting crushing poverty, mental depression, and total family ruin.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Water ponds directly beneath or around the core building, saturating foundations and generating rising damp and mold.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Must be mechanically backfilled with clean compacted red or river soil until the center is level or slightly higher than the perimeter.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 38; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 9
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: dakṣiṇa-paścimonnata-bhūmir gajapṛṣṭheti kīrtitā | āyur-dhana-kulodbhūtā sarvasaukhyakarī nṛṇām ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Elevated in the South, South-West, and West; descending gently toward North, East, and North-East. Emulates an elephant's back (Gajapṛṣṭha), granting immense strength, social honor, long lifespan, and enduring prosperity.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Shields the dwelling from southwest storms and afternoon solar glare while admitting morning sun and northern breezes.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Maintain this natural contour without excavating the southern or western shoulders.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 41; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 11
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: īśāna-pūrva-saṃsthitir unnatā daityapṛṣṭhakā | dravyāyuḥ-suta-nāśāya nityaṃ roga-bhayāvahā ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Elevated in the North-East and North; plunging down toward the South and South-West. Designated Daityapṛṣṭha (Demon back), it reverses cosmic polarity, annihilating wealth, lifespan, and progeny.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Blocks morning sunlight and geomagnetic flux while channeling all runoff into the high-heat SW corner.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Extensive civil earth re-engineering: cut down the NE ridge and use it to fill the SW depression.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 15-18; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 15
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: aratni-mātre khāte tu pūrite tair mṛdādibhiḥ | adhike dravyam uddiṣṭaṃ same madhyamadhīmatā | hīne dāridryam ākhyātaṃ tasmāt hīnaṃ vivarjayet ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Digging a 1-cubit pit and refilling it with the dug earth leaves surplus soil overflowing. Indicates densely preconsolidated soil with low void ratio and high safe bearing capacity; guarantees domestic durability and wealth.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: High relative compaction, low void ratio ($e < 0.5$), minimal risk of settlement under structural foundations.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: None required. Standard shallow isolated footing is sufficient.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 18; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 16
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: hīne dāridryam āpnoti kṣayaṃ vā samupāgatam |
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Excavated earth fails to fill back the pit, sinking into a depression. Indicates porous, highly compressible, loose soil liable to differential structural settlement; causes financial ruin.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: High void ratio ($e > 1.0$), collapsable or organic soil matrix; acute danger of foundation cracking.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Excavate down to hard bedrock or dense stratum; replace loose topsoil with compacted engineered sand/gravel; design raft foundation or under-reamed piles.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 16; Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 20
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: jala-pūrṇa-karte dṛṣṭe prātar dravya-samṛddhidā |
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Water poured into the test pit at sunset remains standing at dawn. Confirms cohesive, impermeable subsoil capable of holding foundation loads without rapid leaching.
rules_matrix.engineering_physical_rationale: Cohesive clayey-silt matrix preventing subterranean erosion or piping failures under water-table fluctuations.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Provide adequate peripheral subsoil plinth drainage to prevent surface dampness.

interpretation: In classical Sthāpatya Veda, the plot (Bhūmi) is not an inert physical surface, but a living bio-energetic organism known as the Vāstu Puruṣa. Analysis of a plot synthesizes macroscopic topography (Bhūmi-Pṛṣṭha: Gajapṛṣṭha vs Daityapṛṣṭha), precise boundary geometry (Kṣetra-Saṃsthāna), geotechnical load-bearing capacity (Garta-pūraṇa and Jala-parīkṣā), solar geometry (Plava / natural slope towards North and East), and street kinetic vectors (Vīthi-śūla). The primary objective is to maximize the absorption of early morning solar ultraviolet-A rays and geomagnetic lines of force (Jaiva-ūrjā) descending from the North-East, while grounding and shielding the dwelling against the harsh infrared thermal and tectonic stresses of the South-West.
variation_note: Classical regional treatises demonstrate deliberate geographical adaptations: 1. Northern & Rajasthani tradition (Viśvakarma Prakāśa, Aparājitapṛcchā) emphasizes high protective boundary walls, deep square compounds, and defense against abrasive desert sandstorms and severe southern heat. 2. Southern Drāviḍa tradition (Mānasāra, Mayamata) focuses on exact mathematical orientation via gnomonic shadow circles (Śaṅku-dig-nirṇaya) and proportional modularity using the Āyādi-ṣaḍvarga formulas. 3. Kerala tradition (Manuṣyālaya Candrikā) is adapted to torrential tropical rainfall; it mandates that natural drainage must slope North-East, enforces uncompromised central open-air courtyards (Nālukettu), and relaxes certain rigid soil color constraints due to ubiquitous laterite soil.

rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Must be permanently sealed. Pump out standing water, fill completely with compacted clean gravel, sand, and sacred clay, and seal with a consecrated granite or marble slab.

rules_matrix.scientific_environmental_rationale: Cavity at the highest stress point of building foundation undermines soil shear strength.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Relocate to WNW; fill cavity with compacted quarry dust and yellow clay.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 5; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 45
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: prāg-udaṅ-nimna-mārgeṇa jala-nirgamanaṃ śubham | dhana-dhānya-karī nityaṃ sarva-roga-haraṃ nṛṇām ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Stormwater and greywater drainage sloping from South/West across the site and discharging out through the North-East or North boundary. Confers health, sustained wealth, and cleanliness.
rules_matrix.scientific_environmental_rationale: Follows the natural geomagnetic and solar drainage slope, preventing stagnant backflows and soil saturation.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Maintain clear, covered inspection chambers.

rules_matrix.element_mahabhuta: Drainage of Wealth into the Abyss
rules_matrix.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 8; Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: nairṛtye jala-niryāṇe dravyāṇāṃ saṅkṣayo bhavet |
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Discharging site drainage or plumbing waste out towards the South-West drains away the accumulated wealth and stability of the family.
rules_matrix.scientific_environmental_rationale: Creates saturated foundation soils in the quadrant that requires highest bearing capacity.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Re-route underground drainage pipes to exit via the North or East perimeters.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 54 (Dakārgala) v. 9-15
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: yadi dṛśyate'rjuna-vṛkṣo valmīka-yutaḥ pradeśa-mātreṇa | tasmāt paścād gamyā sirā bhavaty amṛta-sannibhā ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Varāhamihira's Dakārgala bio-indicators for locating underground aquifers: 1. Arjuna or Jambu tree with a termite mound (Valmīka) to its North indicates sweet water at shallow depth (3-5 Puruṣas / 18-30 ft) to the East or West. 2. Vetasa (reed cane) thriving in dry land confirms an active subterranean vein directly underneath.
rules_matrix.scientific_environmental_rationale: Phreatophytic tree roots (Arjuna, Jamun) penetrate deeply into subsoil aquifers; subterranean termite colonies require constant high relative humidity (90%+) and construct mounds directly above moisture veins.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Utilize these natural bio-indicators to site domestic wells rather than drilling blindly.

rules_matrix.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 54 v. 121-122
rules_matrix.classical_sloka: añjana-mustā-uśīraiḥ sa-lodhra-katakaiḥ kṛtaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ | yoge'nena payāṃsi bhavanti vimalāni sugandhīni ||
rules_matrix.plain_language_explanation: Classical water clarification and purification formula: Combine powdered Kataka seeds (Strychnos potatorum / clearing nut), Mustā root (Cyperus rotundus), Uśīra root (Vetiveria zizanioides / vetiver), Lodhra bark, and Añjana. Added to turbid, brackish, or foul-smelling well water, it clears suspended matter, neutralizes odor, and makes the water sparkling clear, sweet, and safe.
rules_matrix.scientific_environmental_rationale: Kataka seed proteins act as natural polyelectrolyte coagulants that bind colloidal clay particles within minutes (matching modern alum coagulants); Vetiver and Mustā possess powerful antimicrobial essential oils that adsorb volatile sulfides and inhibit bacterial growth.
rules_matrix.classical_remedy: Treat stagnant tanks or wells periodically with Kataka and Vetiver root sachets to maintain biological freshness naturally.

interpretation: In the classical canon of Vedic architecture, water (Jala-tattva) is treated as the primary carrier of prāṇic vitality and financial liquidity. The science of Jala-Vinyāsa operates under a rigorous dual-polarity principle balancing mass and elemental qualities: 1. Subterranean excavations (wells, sumps, borewells) create cavities of low gravitational density, which harmonize with the light, receptive, divine sectors of the North-East, North, and East, but create catastrophic vacuums if dug into the heavy foundational Earth zone of the South-West or the central navel (Brahmasthāna). 2. Conversely, overhead water tanks represent massive static loads (structural deadweight), which harmonize with the South-West and West where ballast is required to anchor the structure, but crush mental and spiritual well-being if placed atop the North-East. 3. Biological sewage (septic tanks) must be strictly isolated to the disposal zones of the West-North-West (WNW), preventing contamination of sacred and magnetic sectors. Furthermore, Varāhamihira's Dakārgala provides an empirically validated science of subterranean hydrology, bio-indicators, and natural coagulation.
variation_note: Significant geographical and regional traditions govern water vāstu: 1. Kerala tradition (Manuṣyālaya Candrikā): In Kerala's high-rainfall maritime climate, digging the domestic well (Kūpa) in the Parjanya or Pūṣan pada is the mandatory first ritual preceding all construction; complex rainwater harvesting channels direct sloped-roof runoff into granite cisterns (Kulam), with strict avoidance of the Karṇa-sūtra (diagonal cords). 2. Western Indian / Rajasthani tradition (Viśvakarma Prakāśa, Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra): In arid climates, subterranean step-wells (Vāpī/Bāoli) and shaded courtyard water cisterns (Taṅkā) were engineered with thick sandstone walls to prevent evaporation. 3. Eastern / Bengal tradition: Village ponds (Pukur) were strategically excavated to the North-East or East of homesteads, serving dual roles as fish nurseries and morning solar reflectors.
